provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Enumerate visible A-repeat/B/C-repeat explanations and require unique continuation output. Removed majority-vote and unchanged-grid fallbacks. Constructor retains original renderer and explicit fixture values, rejects hidden-phase ambiguity. Factory emits concrete growth/stacking edge coordinate expressions; no whole-grid inverse transforms or palette wrappers. Host fixture check found a false reference split at col8 with a single visible C column. Native reference cols are bounded by pre-sampling awide1..2 times1..2, so col<=4; the earlier claim that every relaxed parse was a valid latent was wrong. Enforce this bound in both checker and program. Short-band fixture cols remain unconstrained beyond tile alignment, including3. No fixture labels changed.
draft_notes.limitations: Native motif width1..2, occupied band span1..3, separated bands and tile-aligned A/B boundaries. Rejection sampling1000draws; acceptance requires all visible parses produce the independently drawn label. Direction/palette specialized consistently with episode augmentation. Broader arbitrary tile grammars are outside the current family. Reference boundary col<=4 follows native sampler, not arbitrary suffix-length voting. Explicit references outside this domain are outside admitted scope.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The host counterexample is train pair 0 of the episode. In canonical colours, the reference occupies rows 2-3: columns 0-2 fill both rows, then columns alternate between {lower} and {both}. Each short band is a 2x2 block at columns 0-1.

Two generator latents with identical sampling probability render this exact input:
(a) A = full column, B = full column, C = [{lower},{both}], reference col=2, shorts col=1. Here the shorts continue lower, both, lower, … This is the label.
(b) A = full column, B = full column, C = [{both},{lower}], reference col=1, shorts col=1. Here the shorts continue both, lower, …

Both latents have the same pixel counts, pool sizes and a 1/2 chance of col. The failed factory's likelihood scores were therefore exactly tied, and it kept the first-enumerated parse (E0=2, i.e. reading (b)). The archived token-suffix solver also yields (b).

The label is decided only by a hidden randint (the reference's col). This is not a factory bug that a special case could fix.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: Invisible B/C boundaries can hide which phase begins the repeated continuation. Original random scenes can share inputs but differ in outputs; reject ambiguous phases rather than select by parse count.
